matches.rationale: The ground truth highlights unsupported qualitative behavior claims in the abstract; pred9 notes the paper admits lack of conclusive evidence for emergent behaviors, capturing the same overstatement issue.
Both point out confusion in depth definition between residual blocks and total Dense layers; pred7 directly identifies the inconsistency between Figure 2 and experimental depth references.
No finding identifies missing training regime/learning rate/compute budget details; unmatched.
The ground truth criticizes overstatement of emergent behaviors in Section 4.3; pred9 exposes the same contradiction, quoting the paper’s own admission of no conclusive quantitative evidence.
No finding mentions the fabricated Neumann and Gros (2022) reference.
No finding addresses omission of compute limitation discussion in the conclusion.
No finding specifically identifies exaggerated promotional phrases like 'unlock substantial improvements' in the abstract; the findings focus on numerical mismatches or qualitative overclaim.
Ground truth describes distorted data in Figure 6 overstating joint actor-critic scaling; pred12 points out a specific unsupported 30% improvement claim derived from Figure 6 data.

Ground truth notes that the claim that batch size becomes effective only with depth is contradicted by Figure 7; pred5 captures the tension between claiming effective batch size scaling and marginal/inconsistent improvements.
No finding detects the omission of ethical/carbon footprint discussion in the impact statement.
No finding identifies the promotional claim in the introduction about surpassing width scaling.
Ground truth points to unrealistically large 983× improvement in Appendix Table 1; pred8 challenges the same table’s stated 600× improvement as misleading due to large uncertainty and rounding.
No finding mentions the L2 vs dot-product critic output inconsistency.
No finding addresses missing disclosure of MJX/Brax version discrepancies.

Ground truth says the claim 'CRL is critical' marginalizes other methods; pred10 notes a contradiction between Section 4.4’s claim and Section 4.6’s statement that CRL depth scaling does not help offline, undermining the broad attribution.
No finding identifies inconsistent wall-clock times in the appendix.

Ground truth says deep models qualitatively better behaviors are overgeneralized from limited humanoid evidence; pred9 captures the lack of conclusive evidence for qualitative leaps, matching the same overstatement.
